issues.legal_issue: A person who neither applied for a public appointment nor met its required qualifications cannot maintain a constitutional writ challenging the recruitment rules and appointments when the hereditary office previously held by that person has been abolished and the rules give the person's category the first preference.
material_facts: The appellants had held hereditary village-accountant offices, but the abolition of hereditary village offices had been upheld by the Supreme Court.
The recruitment rules gave first preference to people who had served as village officers, a category that included the appellants.
The appellants did not apply for the new appointments because they lacked the prescribed qualifications.
The appellants challenged the recruitment rules and the selection and appointment of other candidates, seeking to remain in their former posts.
issues.conclusion: The appellants had no right to maintain the writ petitions; the High Court was correct to dismiss them, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Although Article 226 does not specify who may apply, the existence of a right is implicit in invoking its jurisdiction, and a person who is not aggrieved by the alleged discrimination cannot maintain a writ petition. The Court relied on B.R. Shankaranarayana & Ors. v. State of Mysore, which upheld the constitutional validity of the abolition of hereditary village offices, and referred to Gazula Daseratha Rama Rao v. State of A.P. on discrimination based solely on descent. Articles 14 and 16 forbid arbitrary or invidious distinctions but do not bar selective tests or general educational qualifications for public appointments.

rule.if: constitutional_writ_challenging_public_recruitment and hereditary_office_abolition_was_upheld and claimants_did_not_apply and claimants_lacked_required_qualifications and claimants_category_received_first_preference

predicates.constitutional_writ_challenging_public_r: The claimants brought a constitutional writ challenging rules and appointments for public posts.
predicates.hereditary_office_abolition_was_upheld: A court had upheld the abolition of the hereditary public office previously held by the claimants.
predicates.claimants_did_not_apply: The claimants did not apply for the new public appointments.
predicates.claimants_lacked_required_qualifications: The claimants did not possess the qualifications required for the new appointments.
predicates.claimants_category_received_first_prefer: The recruitment rules gave first preference to a category that included the claimants.

issues.definition: When claimants bring a constitutional writ challenging public recruitment, the prior abolition of their hereditary office has been upheld, they did not apply because they lacked the required qualifications, and their category received first preference, they cannot maintain the writ.
